Coinkite Releases Coldcard Security Incident Postmortem as 1,778.84 BTC Stolen From Over 8,600 Addresses Bitcoin hardware wallet maker Coinkite has released its postmortem on Coldcard’s seed-generation flaw, confirming that attackers reconstructed private keys offline rather than compromising the devices. A firmware configuration error disabled the hardware random number generator, causing devices to rely on an insecure pseudorandom number generator. At least 15 independent review and security research efforts between 2021 and 2026 failed to identify the flaw, including a review using OpenAI’s Cybersecurity Harness. Coinkite received 300 loss-related support tickets involving 236 customer accounts, approximately 0.2% of its estimated user base. According to Galaxy Research, 1,778.84 BTC were stolen from over 8,600 addresses, worth approximately $107 million at current prices. Coinkite released patched firmware on July 31 but warned that firmware updates cannot secure previously affected seeds. The attackers remain unidentified, and Coinkite has yet to decide whether to compensate affected customers. — link

X Wins Lawsuit Against Fake Bitcoin News Bot Farm Operators Over Alleged $277,000 Creator Fund Fraud According to UK High Court filings, the court has entered a judgment in default in favor of X against defendants Vivek Kumar Sen and Zamyang Sherpa over their operation of a fake bitcoin news bot farm, after both failed to file an acknowledgment of service or a defense within the prescribed deadlines, with the specific amount of damages and interest to be determined at a subsequent Disposal Hearing. Previously, X filed suit in London in September alleging that the pair operated a nine-account network—including Vivek4real_ and Bitcoin_Teddy—that circulated fabricated breaking news and generated fake engagement to fraudulently collect at least £207,000 ($277,000) from the platform's creator fund. — link

Fidelity Crypto Adds Aave, Chainlink, and Uniswap Tokens, Expanding Supported Assets to Eight According to Cryptobriefing, Fidelity’s cryptocurrency trading platform Fidelity Crypto has added three decentralized finance (DeFi) tokens—Aave (AAVE), Chainlink (LINK), and Uniswap (UNI)—allowing eligible U.S. customers to trade them via Fidelity Crypto accounts, including certain crypto IRA accounts. The additions expand Fidelity Crypto’s supported assets from five to eight—joining Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Litecoin, and its proprietary stablecoin Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD). — link
